note: Works via the Shared Mail Server too: create an AlwaysData mailbox and authenticate on smtp-<username>.alwaysdata.net (SMTP AUTH, e.g. Python smtplib or PHPMailer), then send with a forged From on the hosted domain. MAIL FROM is aligned with the hosted/victim domain (in SPF), so DMARC passes on the SPF branch even under p=reject. Same DKIM behaviour as the Local MTA (signed d=alwaysdata.net s=default, valid, not aligned -> avoids an R_DKIM_NA penalty, DMARC via SPF). Measured 2026-10-30: DMARC PASSES via SPF alignment even at p=reject (Rspamd DMARC_POLICY_ALLOW [example.com,reject], R_SPF_ALLOW, R_DKIM_ALLOW [alwaysdata.net:s=default]), and the spoof is delivered to the Gmail INBOX (not spam).
